full_query: How do I know if its a canker sore versus herpes
sentences: To differentiate between a canker sore and a herpes lesion, consider the following characteristics
Canker sores (aphthous ulcers) typically occur inside the mouth on the soft tissues, such as the inner cheeks, lips, tongue, or the base of the gums
Herpes lesions (caused by herpes simplex virus) often appear on the lips (cold sores) or around the mouth, but can also occur inside the mouth, particularly on the hard palate or gums
Canker sores are usually small, round or oval, with a white or yellow center and a red border
Herpes lesions start as small, fluid-filled blisters that eventually burst and form painful ulcers
Canker sores are typically painful, especially when eating or talking, but do not cause systemic symptoms
Herpes lesions can be painful and may be preceded by a tingling or burning sensation
They can also be associated with systemic symptoms such as fever, swollen lymph nodes, and malaise
Canker sores are not caused by a virus and are not contagious
They can be triggered by factors such as stress, minor mouth injuries, acidic or spicy foods, and certain medical conditions
Herpes lesions are caused by the herpes simplex virus, which remains dormant in the body and can reactivate, leading to recurrent outbreaks
Triggers include stress, illness, sunlight, and hormonal changes
Canker sores are usually diagnosed based on clinical appearance and history
No specific tests are typically required

Herpes lesions can be diagnosed through clinical examination, but confirmation may require laboratory tests such as viral culture, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), or serologic tests for herpes simplex virus antibodies
